shifts: <list[str], length num_shifts> Named work shifts available in the scheduling horizon.
skills: <list[str], length num_skills> Named skills that nurses may possess and perform during shifts.

nurses.skills: <list[str]> Skills this nurse is qualified to perform.

preferences.day: <int> Day number (1-indexed) the preference applies to.
preferences.shift: <str> Shift name the preference refers to, or 'None' for day-off preferences.
preferences.penalty: <int> Cost incurred if this preference is not honored.

weekend_definition: <str> Which days of the week constitute a weekend.

weekends.week: <int> Week number (1-indexed) this weekend belongs to.
weekends.saturday: <int> Day number (1-indexed) of Saturday in this weekend.
weekends.sunday: <int> Day number (1-indexed) of Sunday in this weekend.

{shift}.{skill}: <int> Minimum number of nurses with this skill required on this shift and day.

unsatisfied_demand_penalty: <int> Cost per unit of unmet demand across day-shift-skill combinations.

forbidden_patterns.pattern: <list[list[str]], shape [pattern_length][2]> Sequence of consecutive-day [day_type, shift] pairs that must never appear in any nurse's schedule.
forbidden_patterns.description: <str> Human-readable explanation of the forbidden pattern.

hard_constraints.skill_requirement: <bool> Whether nurses may only perform skills they possess.
hard_constraints.single_assignment_per_day: <bool> Whether each nurse must be assigned exactly one shift per day.
hard_constraints.demand_equality: <bool, optional> If true, staffing must equal demand exactly and demand slack is disabled.

total_working_days.min: <int> Minimum number of days each nurse should work over the horizon.
total_working_days.max: <int> Maximum number of days each nurse should work over the horizon.
total_working_days.penalty_under: <int> Cost per day below the minimum working-day target.
total_working_days.penalty_over: <int> Cost per day above the maximum working-day target.

total_worked_weekends.max: <int> Maximum number of weekends each nurse should work.
total_worked_weekends.penalty: <int> Cost per weekend worked above the maximum.

consecutive_working_days.min: <int> Minimum length of any unbroken streak of working days.
consecutive_working_days.max: <int> Maximum length of any unbroken streak of working days.
consecutive_working_days.penalty_under: <int> Cost per occurrence of a working streak shorter than the minimum.
consecutive_working_days.penalty_over: <int> Cost per day a working streak exceeds the maximum.

consecutive_days_off.min: <int> Minimum length of any unbroken streak of rest days.
consecutive_days_off.max: <int> Maximum length of any unbroken streak of rest days.
consecutive_days_off.penalty_under: <int> Cost per occurrence of a rest streak shorter than the minimum.
consecutive_days_off.penalty_over: <int> Cost per day a rest streak exceeds the maximum.

consecutive_same_shift.max: <int> Maximum number of consecutive days a nurse may be assigned the same work shift.
consecutive_same_shift.penalty: <int> Cost per day a same-shift streak exceeds the maximum.

consecutive_worked_weekends.max: <int> Maximum number of consecutive weekends a nurse may work.
consecutive_worked_weekends.penalty: <int> Cost per weekend a consecutive-weekend streak exceeds the maximum.

identical_weekend.enabled: <bool> Whether the identical-weekend rule is active.
identical_weekend.penalty: <int> Cost incurred when the shifts on the days named by a weekend record are not all identical.

soft_constraints.skill_requirement_penalty: <int, optional> Cost per worked day assigned to a skill the nurse does not possess when skill possession is soft.
soft_constraints.forbidden_patterns: <list[object], optional> Soft forbidden shift sequences with per-occurrence penalties.
soft_constraints.preferences_penalty: <bool or number, optional> Enables the penalty stored on each unmet nurse preference.
